parts.instructions: This paper contains 100 multiple-choice questions only. You must answer all of them; each question carries 1 point. There is only one best answer for each question: choose it and blacken its letter on the answer sheet.

exam.answer_key_note: No official key exists. There are no Social Studies textbooks, so every answer was solved independently and checked against the Eritrean MoE Geography (G9–12), History (G9–12) and Business & Economics (G10–12) textbooks (extracted text with page markers). Items with two defensible options accept both and carry a review_flag.

questions.stem: The branch of human geography that studies the effect of human culture on the landscape is
explanation_steps: The textbook (fields of human geography): 'Cultural Geography: the study of the effect of human culture on the landscape. It examines the location and spread of beliefs, customs and other cultural characteristics.'
Population geography studies population; economic geography studies economic activities. Answer: C.
tips: The stem copies the textbook definition word for word – look for the key word 'culture'.

similar_questions.stem: The branch of human geography that studies the composition, growth, distribution and migration of people is
explanation_steps: Textbook: 'Population Geography: the study of human populations; their composition, growth, distribution, and migration.'
Answer: B.

textbook_ref.unit: Unit 1 – The Subject Matter of Geography

questions.stem: The planet popularly known as the ‘Red Planet’ is
explanation_steps: Mars is one of the four inner (terrestrial) planets – Mercury, Venus, Earth and Mars – listed in the textbook.
Its surface is covered with reddish iron-oxide dust, so it looks red and is called the 'Red Planet'. Answer: D.
tips: Mercury = nearest the sun; Venus = hottest/brightest; Jupiter = largest; Saturn = rings; Mars = red.

similar_questions.stem: The largest planet of the solar system is
explanation_steps: Jupiter is the largest of the outer 'giant' planets (and of all planets).
Answer: C.

textbook_ref.note: The textbook lists Mars among the inner planets but does not use the nickname 'Red Planet' (general knowledge).

questions.stem: Which of the following factors is <u>not</u> an element of weather?
explanation_steps: The elements of weather and climate in the textbook are temperature, air pressure, wind, humidity and precipitation.
All four listed factors (A–D) are elements, so none of them is 'not an element'. Answer: E.
tips: Elements = what is measured (temperature, pressure, wind, humidity, precipitation). Controls/factors = what causes differences (latitude, altitude, distance from sea, ocean currents).

similar_questions.stem: Which of the following is a factor (control) of climate rather than an element of weather?
explanation_steps: Altitude affects temperature and rainfall but is not itself measured as weather.
Answer: C.

additional_textbook_refs.section: 3.1 Introduction – elements and factors of climate

questions.stem: The coastal parts of Eritrea receive rain during
explanation_steps: The textbook: during winter the ITCZ moves south of Eritrea; the north-east trade winds blow across the Red Sea, pick up moisture and bring winter rain to the eastern escarpment and coastal areas.
'In Eritrea the eastern lowlands and eastern escarpments get winter rainfall from the northeast trade winds.' Answer: A.
tips: Highlands and western lowlands = summer (kremti) rain; coast and eastern escarpment = winter rain (NE trades from the Red Sea).

similar_questions.stem: The main rainy season of the Eritrean highlands, locally called 'kremti', occurs in
explanation_steps: Summer rain comes when the ITCZ moves north and moist south-westerly winds reach Eritrea.
Answer: B.

textbook_ref.section: 3.3 Seasons and rainfall in Eritrea – winter rain

questions.stem: The smallest Zoba in Eritrea is
explanation_steps: The textbook table of administrative zones gives the areas: Maekel 1,400 km², Debub 9,709 km², Anseba 22,120 km², Southern Red Sea 23,384 km², Northern Red Sea 33,178 km², Gash-Barka about 34,500 km².
Maekel (Central Zone, centre Asmara) is by far the smallest. Answer: A.
tips: Smallest = Maekel; largest = Gash-Barka. Maekel is small in area but the most densely populated.

similar_questions.stem: Which zoba of Eritrea has the largest surface area?
explanation_steps: From the same table: Gash-Barka is the largest (≈34,500 km²).
Answer: D.

textbook_ref.unit: Unit 6 – Strategic Position, Size and Shape of Eritrea

questions.stem: The tiny ice crystals formed on and near the ground, when temperature falls below freezing point is known as
explanation_steps: The textbook: 'Frost is made up of ice crystals formed near the ground when the temperature is below freezing point. These are seen on window panes, grasses, pavements and on the ground.'
Dew is liquid water droplets formed above 0 °C. Answer: A.
tips: Below 0 °C → frost (ice); above 0 °C → dew (water droplets); fog/mist = condensation suspended in the air.

similar_questions.stem: Water droplets that condense on grass when air cools to its dew point (above 0 °C) are called
explanation_steps: When air cools to the dew point, water vapour condenses as dew on cool surfaces.
Answer: B.

textbook_ref.section: 3.7 Humidity and forms of condensation – frost

questions.stem: Asmara is located
explanation_steps: The textbook divides the Eritrean highlands into regions; the Central Plateau extends from Adi Tekelezan–Zaghir to the Dekemhare–Tera Emni road and includes Asmara.
Asmara (≈2,300 m) sits on this flat, fertile plateau. Answer: A.
tips: Asmara, Mendefera and Adi Keih are plateau towns; Ghindae and Nefasit are on the eastern escarpment.

similar_questions.stem: Which of the following towns is found on the eastern escarpment of Eritrea?
explanation_steps: Ghindae lies on the eastern escarpment between Asmara and Massawa.
Answer: C.

textbook_ref.unit: Unit 7 – Relief and Drainage Systems in Eritrea
textbook_ref.section: 7.1 Relief of Eritrea – the Central Plateau

questions.stem: The climate of a place is affected by its
explanation_steps: The textbook: 'The factors are latitude, ocean currents, topography, altitude, and more.' Latitude and altitude are the most important factors for Eritrea.
Distance from the sea (continentality) and the distribution of land and water also control temperature and rainfall. All four are climatic factors. Answer: E.
tips: Remember the controls of climate: latitude, altitude, distance from the sea, ocean currents, relief, prevailing winds, land–water distribution.

similar_questions.stem: Temperature decreases with height at an average rate of about
explanation_steps: Normal lapse rate = 6.5 °C per 1000 m – the reason altitude is a major climatic control.
Answer: C.

questions.stem: The climatic region with the lowest rainfall is the
explanation_steps: Dry climates are divided into desert (arid) and semi-desert (steppe). Deserts receive the least rainfall (generally under 250 mm a year, often much less); semi-deserts receive a little more.
Savannah (tropical grassland) and temperate climates are much wetter. Answer: A.
tips: Rainfall order (driest first): desert < semi-desert (steppe) < savannah < monsoon < equatorial.

similar_questions.stem: A dry climate in which evaporation exceeds precipitation but short grass can grow (e.g. the Sahel) is
explanation_steps: Semi-deserts/steppes lie between deserts and savannahs and have slightly more rain than deserts.
Answer: B.

textbook_ref.unit: Unit 1 – Major Types of World Climates

questions.stem: Among the planets in the solar system, the nearest to the sun is
explanation_steps: The textbook lists the inner planets in order from the sun: Mercury, Venus, Earth and Mars.
Mercury is the first, nearest the sun. Answer: A.
tips: Order: My Very Easy Method Just Speeds Up Naming – Mercury, Venus, Earth, Mars, Jupiter, Saturn, Uranus, Neptune.

similar_questions.stem: Which planet lies between Venus and Mars?
explanation_steps: Order: Mercury, Venus, Earth, Mars.
Answer: B.

questions.stem: The soils on river flood plains are good for agriculture because

options.A: the area is rich with surface and ground water.
options.C: the flat topography is easy to till.

explanation_steps: The textbook: 'a flood plain is a wide and flat plain built up by alluvium deposited on the valley floor after flooding. Flood plains have fertile soil.'
They also have plentiful surface and ground water, deep (thick) deposits, flat land that is easy to plough and little erosion. All the options apply. Answer: E.
tips: Flood plains and deltas (Nile, Ganges) support dense farming populations – deep, fertile alluvium on flat, well-watered land.

similar_questions.stem: Fine fertile material deposited by rivers on their flood plains is called
explanation_steps: River-deposited sediment = alluvium; wind-deposited = loess; glacier-deposited = moraine.
Answer: B.

textbook_ref.unit: Unit 2 – Gradation by Rivers and Winds

questions.stem: The method of soil conservation that involves planting of trees over a flat area is
explanation_steps: The textbook: 'Planting of shelter belts: Trees are often planted across a flat region that is exposed to wind erosion. The trees break the force of the wind and thus protect the soil from being eroded.'
Terracing and contour ploughing are for slopes. Answer: E.
tips: Flat, windy land → shelter belts (wind-breaks). Slopes → terraces, contour ploughing, check dams.

similar_questions.stem: Cutting steep slopes into a series of wide steps on which crops are grown is called
explanation_steps: Textbook: 'Steep slopes are cut into a series of wide steps… called terraces.'
Answer: B.

questions.stem: At present, the two most populous countries in the world are
explanation_steps: The textbook: 'Out of a 4.1 billion population of Asia, about 2.5 billion or 62% live in China and India alone' (Table 3.4, ten most populated countries).
China and India each have well over a billion people. Answer: C.
tips: Since 2023 India has overtaken China as the most populous country – but the pair China and India is still the top two.

similar_questions.stem: The third most populous country in the world is
explanation_steps: After India and China, the USA (≈330+ million) ranks third.
Answer: B.

textbook_ref.section: 3.3.2 The spatial pattern of world population distribution

questions.stem: Which of the following countries is most dependent on River Nile?
explanation_steps: Egypt is almost entirely desert; nearly all its people, farms and water supply are on the Nile valley and delta (about 95 % of its water comes from the Nile).
The upstream countries receive rainfall of their own. Answer: D.
tips: Herodotus called Egypt 'the gift of the Nile'.

similar_questions.stem: The Nile flows into the
explanation_steps: The Nile forms a delta in northern Egypt and enters the Mediterranean.
Answer: C.

textbook_ref.section: 3.3.1 Factors affecting population distribution – river deltas
textbook_ref.note: The textbook mentions the Nile delta and dense settlement in Egypt; Egypt's dependence on the Nile is general knowledge.

questions.stem: Which of the following is a major driving force for a country’s development?
explanation_steps: The Geography textbook (concept of development): 'Education is the major driving force for development. The pace of development depends on the quality of' the human resources.
Capital, labour and raw materials are needed too, but the textbook names education as the major driving force. Answer: C.
tips: When several options sound right, choose the one the textbook states in the same words.

similar_questions.stem: Money set aside from income that becomes available for investment in development programmes is
explanation_steps: Textbook: 'investment comes from saving' – people postpone consumption and save.
Answer: B.

questions.stem: A natural hazard that occurs in the Danakil area is
explanation_steps: The Danakil Depression lies on the Red Sea / East African rift, a divergent plate boundary where the crust is being pulled apart.
The textbook names Dubbi, Jalua and Alid in the eastern lowlands as active volcanoes; rifting also produces frequent earthquakes (e.g. the 2011 Nabro eruption and its earthquakes).
Both earthquakes and volcanic eruptions occur there. Answer: E.
tips: Rift valley = tectonically active: earthquakes + volcanoes together.

similar_questions.stem: Which of the following is an active volcano in the eastern lowlands of Eritrea?
explanation_steps: Textbook: 'Dubbi, Jalua and Alid in the eastern lowlands are examples of active volcanoes.'
Answer: B.

additional_textbook_refs.section: 1.2 Geological history – Danakil Depression and rifting

questions.stem: Erosion by wind is more common in
explanation_steps: The textbook: 'Wind erosion is more effective and powerful in arid areas where there is an absence of vegetation.'
Overgrazed land has lost its plant cover, so loose dry soil is also blown away. Vegetation-covered areas (A, B) are protected. Answer: E.
tips: Wind erosion needs dry, loose soil and no plant cover: deserts and overgrazed land.

similar_questions.stem: Which of the following best protects farmland from wind erosion?
explanation_steps: Shelter belts reduce wind speed near the ground.
Answer: C.

textbook_ref.unit: Unit 2 – Gradation by Rivers and Winds

questions.stem: The depositional feature that is found at the mouth of a river is
explanation_steps: Where a river enters a sea or lake it slows down and deposits its load at its mouth, building a delta (e.g. the Nile and Niger deltas).
Flood plains form along the lower course, alluvial fans at the foot of mountains, beaches by waves and barchans by wind. Answer: A.
tips: Mouth of river = delta; foot of mountain = alluvial fan; desert = barchan.

similar_questions.stem: A fan-shaped deposit formed where a mountain stream reaches flat land is
explanation_steps: The sudden drop in gradient makes the stream deposit a cone/fan of alluvium.
Answer: B.

textbook_ref.unit: Unit 2 – Gradation by Rivers and Winds

questions.stem: Which of the following towns is <u>not</u> in the coastal area of Eritrea?
explanation_steps: Aseb (port), Gelaelo, Irafaile and Hirgigo are coastal settlements; the textbook names Hirgigo and Irafaile among the fishing villages south of Massawa.
Ghindae is on the eastern escarpment on the Asmara–Massawa road, about 50 km inland. Answer: E.
tips: Coastal: Massawa, Hirgigo, Zula, Irafaile, Gelaelo, Tio, Edd, Aseb. Escarpment: Ghindae, Nefasit.

similar_questions.stem: Which of the following is a port town of Eritrea?
explanation_steps: Eritrea's ports are Massawa and Assab.
Answer: B.

questions.stem: Which of the following countries is the smallest in geographical size?
explanation_steps: Approximate areas: Djibouti ≈ 23,200 km²; Yemen ≈ 528,000 km²; South Sudan ≈ 620,000 km²; Ethiopia ≈ 1.1 million km²; Sudan ≈ 1.9 million km².
Djibouti is the smallest (smaller even than Eritrea, ≈124,000 km²). Answer: C.
tips: The textbook review question: 'The total surface area of Eritrea is smaller than A. Djibouti…' – Eritrea is larger than Djibouti, Rwanda and Burundi.

similar_questions.stem: Which of Eritrea's neighbours is the largest in area?
explanation_steps: Sudan (≈1.9 million km²) is larger than Ethiopia (≈1.1 million km²).
Answer: C.

textbook_ref.unit: Unit 6 – Strategic Position, Size and Shape of Eritrea
textbook_ref.section: 6.3 The size and shape of Eritrea
textbook_ref.note: The textbook compares Eritrea's area with other countries (review questions p.121); the areas of the neighbours are general knowledge.

questions.stem: The Anseba Highlands are mainly covered by
explanation_steps: The textbook: 'The Upper Anseba Highlands are found on both sides of the Anseba River. The landscape is dominated by granite rocks.'
The Geology unit also calls upper Anseba (Adi Gebru to Keren) 'the greatest outcrops of granite' of the Precambrian basement. Answer: B.
tips: Anseba = granite (Precambrian basement); plateau around Asmara–Adi Keih = Tertiary basalt; Adigrat/Enticho = sandstone.

similar_questions.stem: The oldest rocks of Eritrea, exposed in places such as Upper Anseba and Barentu, belong to the
explanation_steps: Textbook: Precambrian basement outcrops include upper Anseba, Halhal, Mensae and the Barentu area.
Answer: C.

textbook_ref.unit: Unit 7 – Relief and Drainage Systems in Eritrea

questions.stem: Of the following, a country with the least occurrence of earthquakes is
explanation_steps: Earthquakes are concentrated along plate boundaries: Chile, Japan and Indonesia lie on the Pacific 'Ring of Fire' (convergent boundaries) and Italy on the Africa–Eurasia collision zone.
Chad lies in the stable interior of the African plate (the Chad basin), far from any plate boundary. Answer: C.
tips: Plate boundary → earthquakes/volcanoes; stable plate interior (shield/basin) → few earthquakes.

similar_questions.stem: Most of the world's active volcanoes and earthquakes are found along the
explanation_steps: The Pacific Ring of Fire follows convergent plate margins around the Pacific.
Answer: B.

textbook_ref.note: The textbook explains plate boundaries; the earthquake record of the individual countries is general knowledge.

questions.stem: In Eritrea, there is a critical shortage of rain in the
explanation_steps: The Eastern Lowlands (coastal plains, Danakil) are hot deserts with very little rainfall (often below 200 mm a year).
The highlands receive the summer (kremti) rains. Answer: C.
tips: Eritrea's driest region = Eastern Lowlands (Denkalia); wettest = green belt of the eastern escarpment (up to 1000 mm).

similar_questions.stem: The part of Eritrea that receives up to 1000 mm of rain because it gets both summer and winter rain is the

options.B: Green Belt of the eastern escarpment

explanation_steps: Textbook: in the Green Belt (Filfil, Solomuna, Mirara, Sabur, Fiche, Moge'o) rainfall reaches 1000 mm.
Answer: B.

additional_textbook_refs.unit: Unit 7 – Relief and Drainage Systems in Eritrea

questions.stem: Which of the following is the most common type of subsistence farming in rural Eritrea?
explanation_steps: The textbook: 'The type of production is mainly subsistence, and the major crops include sorghum, millet, barley, wheat, taff and pulses.' Farmers mainly produce for their own consumption; small-scale irrigation is limited.
Rain-fed crop (cereal) farming is the most common. Answer: A.
tips: Coffee, fruit and tobacco are cash crops grown in small areas.

similar_questions.stem: The central highlands and south-western lowlands of Eritrea are important mainly for
explanation_steps: Textbook: 'The central Highlands and south-western Lowlands are the most important regions for agriculture.'
Answer: C.

questions.stem: The two most densely populated zobas in Eritrea are

options.D: Gash Barka and Debubawi Keih Bahri.
options.E: Gash Barka and Semienawi Keih Bahri.

explanation_steps: The textbook: 'The most densely populated Zobas – Maekel and Debub – have the lowest number of cattle', while Gash Barka is 'sparsely populated'.
The Tigrinya, the largest ethnic group, live mainly in Maekel and Debub. Answer: C.
tips: Highland zobas (cool, fertile, reliable rain) are densely populated; lowland zobas are sparsely populated.

similar_questions.stem: Which zoba of Eritrea has the largest share of the country's livestock?
explanation_steps: Textbook: 48 % of the cattle and 37 % of the goats are in the sparsely populated Zoba Gash Barka.
Answer: C.

questions.stem: In Eritrea, coffee grows mainly around
explanation_steps: Coffee needs high rainfall and mild temperatures. The Green Belt of the eastern escarpment (Filfil, Solomuna, Mirara, Sabur, Fiche, Moge'o) gets up to 1000 mm of rain from both summer and winter rain.
The textbook notes that in this area 'coffee and citrus fruits are cultivated for economic reasons'. Answer: A.
tips: Coffee = wettest part of Eritrea = Green Belt (Filfil/Fishe/Mirara).

similar_questions.stem: The humid lowland woodland of Eritrea, with rainfall of 800–1300 mm, extends across
explanation_steps: Textbook: this vegetation 'extends from the Bizen and Ghindae area up to Geleb and across Filfil, Solomuna, Sabour, Mirara, Fitche and Meg'o'.
Answer: B.

textbook_ref.unit: Unit 4 – Natural Vegetation and Wildlife in Eritrea
textbook_ref.section: 4.4 Proposed national parks – Green Belt (coffee and citrus)

questions.review_flag: The textbook places coffee in the Green Belt (Filfil–Mirara–Fiche area) but does not name 'Fishe-Mirara' as the coffee area explicitly; A is the only wet escarpment site among the options.

questions.stem: Modern industry in Eritrea started and developed during the ______ period.
explanation_steps: The textbook: the Italians established factories to produce consumer goods for their nationals and to make Eritrea a market and a source of raw materials; during Italian rule 'the most important transformation involved large-scale urbanization, transportation infrastructure and industrialization'.
Industry expanded further in the 1930s–40s, but it began in the Italian period. Answer: B.
tips: Italian period: roads, railway, ports, factories, towns. Federal period: Ethiopia dismantled and moved industries.

similar_questions.stem: Why did Eritrean industry decline rapidly after the 1950s?

options.A: Because of the discovery of oil
options.B: Because Ethiopia moved and dismantled industries after annexing Eritrea
options.C: Because of a British ban on factories
options.D: Because of a lack of raw materials only
options.E: Because of the Suez Canal closure

explanation_steps: Textbook: 'the industrial sector declined rapidly following Ethiopia…' (annexation and removal of industries).
Answer: B.

questions.stem: The most common type of transport system in Eritrea is
explanation_steps: The textbook describes Eritrea's road network (built mainly 1934–1939, primary, secondary and feeder roads, with new all-weather roads since independence) as the backbone of the transport system.
The railway is only a short heritage line; sea and air carry mainly foreign trade and passengers. Answer: D.
tips: Most goods and people inside Eritrea move by road (buses and trucks).

similar_questions.stem: The existing road network of Eritrea was built mainly during
explanation_steps: Textbook: 'The existing road network of Eritrea was built during the Italian period between 1934 and 1939.'
Answer: B.

questions.stem: Which of the following is the least urbanized continent in the world?
explanation_steps: The textbook: 'Africa and the rest of Asia have the highest percentages of their population living in rural areas', while North America, Western Europe and East Asia are highly urbanized.
Africa has the lowest share of urban population (about 40 %). Answer: A.
tips: Most urbanized: North America, South America, Europe (>75 %). Least: Africa, then Asia.

similar_questions.stem: About what share of Eritrea's population lives in urban areas according to the Grade 12 textbook?
explanation_steps: Textbook Unit 7: 'About 21 % of the population of Eritrea lives in urban areas.'
Answer: B.

questions.stem: Which of the following is <u>not</u> an effect of the Earth’s rotation?

options.D: The apparent movement of the sun and moon from east to west

explanation_steps: The textbook lists the effects of rotation: day and night, the apparent movement of the sun, differences in local time, deflection of winds and ocean currents, tides.
Seasons are caused by the earth's revolution around the sun together with the tilt of its axis. Answer: A.
tips: Rotation (24 h) → day/night, time, Coriolis. Revolution (365¼ days) + tilt → seasons, changing day length.

similar_questions.stem: The seasons are caused by

options.B: the revolution of the earth and the tilt of its axis
options.E: the distance of the earth from the sun only

explanation_steps: The overhead sun shifts between the tropics as the tilted earth revolves.
Answer: B.

questions.stem: Reduction in forest cover in Eritrea has been caused by all of the following <u>except</u>
explanation_steps: The textbook's causes of deforestation in Eritrea: thirty years of war; clearing forests to expand agriculture; felling trees for fuel and timber to construct houses; concessions for charcoal and fuel wood; recurrent drought that caused trees to dry; overgrazing and rapid urbanization.
A, B and C are human activities listed directly; overgrazing links to pastoralism (D).

Increased aridity is usually treated as a RESULT of deforestation, so E is the intended 'except'. But the textbook does list 'recurrent drought' as a cause, so E is not clearly wrong either. Keyed E; D is also accepted.
tips: In 'except' questions choose the option that is a consequence rather than a cause.

similar_questions.stem: Which of the following is a consequence (effect) of deforestation in Eritrea?

options.A: Increased flooding and siltation of dams

explanation_steps: Textbook: 'Loss of forest cover in the country has led to increased flooding, faster siltation…'
Answer: A.

textbook_ref.unit: Unit 4 – Natural Vegetation and Wildlife in Eritrea

questions.review_flag: No option is clearly not a cause: the textbook lists drought ('recurrent drought caused trees to dry') and overgrazing as causes as well as cutting, clearing and fuel wood. Keyed E (aridity usually taught as an effect); D (pastoralism) accepted. Teacher decision.

questions.stem: One of the following does <u>not</u> cause soil erosion.

options.E: Intense rain after long dry period

explanation_steps: The textbook's main causes of soil degradation in Eritrea are steep slopes, deforestation, overgrazing and poor farming practices (plus drought and heavy, intense rainfall on bare ground).
Rural settlement in itself is not listed as a cause of soil erosion. Answer: D.
tips: Causes: steep slopes, heavy rain on bare soil, deforestation, overgrazing, poor farming (ploughing up and down slopes).

similar_questions.stem: Eritrea loses on average about how many tons of soil per hectare per year?
explanation_steps: Textbook: 'On the average, Eritrea loses 15–20 tons of soil per hectare in a year', up to 100 tons in places.
Answer: B.

questions.stem: The most widely used source of energy in the developing countries is
explanation_steps: In most developing countries households cook and heat with fuel wood, charcoal, dung and crop residues – biomass.
The textbook for Eritrea: 'the largest proportion of total energy consumption is provided by biomass followed by petroleum.' Answer: A.
tips: Biomass = wood, charcoal, dung, crop residue – the main fuel of rural Africa and a cause of deforestation.

similar_questions.stem: After biomass, the second largest source of energy consumed in Eritrea is
explanation_steps: Textbook: biomass followed by petroleum.
Answer: B.

questions.stem: The population of the developed countries is characterized by

options.C: high proportion in the old age group.

explanation_steps: Developed countries have low birth and death rates, long life expectancy and small families.
The textbook lists the aging population (a rising share of older people) and a small workforce as problems of developed countries. So both B and C apply. Answer: E.
tips: Developed = low birth rate, low death rate, many old people (constrictive pyramid). Developing = high birth rate, young population (expansive pyramid).

similar_questions.stem: A population pyramid with a broad base and narrow top indicates

options.B: a high birth rate and young population

explanation_steps: A broad base = many children = high birth rate (expansive pyramid).
Answer: B.

questions.stem: Eritrea has a strategic location because of

options.A: its position along the Red Sea Coast.
options.B: its nearness to the oil rich Middle East.
options.C: it is found along important sea trade routes.
options.D: the geopolitics of the Horn of Africa.

explanation_steps: The textbook: most commercial lines to Europe and the Mediterranean from the Persian Gulf, East Africa and Asia pass through the Red Sea, linking the Indian Ocean and the Suez Canal; Eritrea lies along its south-western shore near the Bab el Mandeb, close to the oil-rich Middle East and in the geopolitically important Horn of Africa.
All four reasons are correct. Answer: E.
tips: Strategic = important for trade, oil routes and military/political control.

similar_questions.stem: The strait at the southern entrance of the Red Sea, near Eritrea, is
explanation_steps: The Bab el Mandeb connects the Red Sea with the Gulf of Aden.
Answer: B.

textbook_ref.unit: Unit 6 – Strategic Position, Size and Shape of Eritrea

questions.stem: Which of the following statements is <u>not</u> true of the early Roman Republic?

options.A: The patricians were wealthy land owners.
options.B: The plebeians had lower status than the patricians.
options.D: Intermarriage between the patricians and plebeians was forbidden.

explanation_steps: The textbook: 'The patricians were wealthy landowners, who became Rome's ruling class… In the early Roman Republic, the plebeians had lower status than the patricians. Intermarriage between members of both groups was forbidden.'
It concludes: 'In practice, however, the wealthy citizens dominated Roman society. Therefore, the Roman Republic was not a democracy.'
A, B and D are true; C is not. Answer: C.
tips: Option E ('All except C') would mean A, B and D are false – the opposite of the textbook.

similar_questions.stem: In the Roman Republic the Senate was made up of

options.A: 300 elected patricians who served for life

explanation_steps: Textbook: the Senate 'was composed of 300 elected patricians who served for life'.
Answer: A.

questions.stem: Identify the <u>incorrect</u> statement.

options.A: The first Agew migration to Eritrea took place by the second half of the 10th Century.
options.B: Debarua was the Capital of Midri-Bahri.
